header: Date/Time: 2025-07-22 15:00 PT; Duration: ~45 minutes; Location: Zoom; Recording: enabled; Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Tara Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Samir Patel (Summit Bank - Head MLOps), Karen Li (CISO), Daniel Cho (Infra Eng), Priya Rao (Product)
summary: Discovery call focused on Summit Bank's requirement for an air-gapped on-prem Redwood Private deployment in a highly regulated banking environment. Covered hardware constraints, offline update process, KMS/HSM integration, network isolation, security reviews (SOC2/ISO), and pilot success criteria. Agreed next steps: share deployment checklist, BOM guidance, pricing bands, and schedule sizing workshop.
transcript:
[00:00] Lina Park (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we can do quick intros. I'm Lina, I'm the AE working with Summit Bank. Marco is our systems SE.
[00:06] Samir Patel (Summit Bank): Hi all, Samir here, thanks.
[00:09] Karen Li (Summit Bank - CISO): Karen, CISO.
[00:11] Daniel Cho: Daniel, infra. Priya on my side will chime if needed.
[00:15] Marco Diaz (Redwood SE): Hi team. I know you sent over the initial RFP note, so we'll go through how Redwood Private can run in an air-gapped on-prem setup and surface some questions.
[00:22] Priya Rao (Summit Bank): Thanks. Our main thing: we need the whole stack offline, certified vendors, and a clear offline update path because banking regulators require no external egress.
[00:31] Lina: Totally understood. Quick context question — are you inclined toward hosting with Redwood hosted or Dedicated, or is Private/on-prem mandatory?
[00:36] Samir: Private only. Our corp policy disallows outbound connections from production to public cloud for model inference. It's a hard constraint.
[00:42] Karen: And we need HSM-backed key management and full audit logs retained for at least seven years per the compliance team.
[00:49] Marco: Understood. Our Redwood Private product supports HSM/KMS integrations and can operate in a fully air-gapped mode. There are two typical approaches: 1) fully offline installer image we ship to your secure facility and 2) a staged import process where we provide signed bundles that your infra team ingests. Both avoid runtime egress.
[01:05] Daniel: Signed bundles sounds good. How do you handle model updates or security patches if we can't connect to your control plane?
[01:12] Marco: For air-gapped, updates are delivered as cryptographically-signed artifacts. You'd pull them into your air-gapped environment via a USB or secure transfer approved by your ops team. We provide a verification tool to validate signatures and a runbook for staged rollouts. There's also an offline admin console you can run on a jump box.
[01:28] Priya: Are there any telemetry or metrics that leave the environment?
[01:31] Tara Nguyen (Redwood CSM): By default, telemetry is disabled in air-gapped deployments. We can enable local metrics collection only, which stores to your internal observability stack (e.g., Prometheus). No data leaves unless you explicitly configure export.
[01:41] Karen: KMS/HSM integration — we use an on-prem Thales HSM. Does Redwood support that?
[01:45] Marco: Yes. We have integrations for PKCS#11 HSMs and can work with Thales or other supported vendors. Keys remain in the HSM; the inference runtime uses a key reference. We'll need access to your security team to validate the integration during onboarding.
[01:56] Samir: Next, hardware. Our procurement wants a BOM. We have two constraints: rack space and GPU availability. We currently plan NVidia A100 80GB, but procurement says some data centers might only have 40GB A100s or H100s next quarter.
[02:10] Lina: Ok. We typically size per expected qps and model context length. Marco, do you want to walk through sizing guidance?
[02:16] Marco: Sure. For a production LLM serving 8 to 12k tokens per minute and 95th percentile latency of ~300ms, we recommend either: (a) A cluster of 4 x A100-80GB with the Redwood runtime and quantized weights, or (b) If using A100-40GB, increase to 6 nodes and consider pipeline parallelism. H100s generally give better perf if available. Also we can support CPU-only for embeddings but that's slower.
[02:40] Daniel: We might be limited to 40GB, so the 6-node suggestion is helpful. Any special networking like RDMA requirements?
[02:46] Marco: We support both gRPC and our internal fast path. For multi-node KV cache and sharding we recommend 100Gbps RDMA or equivalent for low tail latency. But for single-node deployments that's not required.
[02:58] Priya: On the compliance side, can you provide SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts?
[03:03] Lina: Yes, we will share our SOC2 report and ISO summary. For Private installs we also provide a runbook and a scope document indicating which controls are client-managed and which are Redwood-managed.
[03:13] Karen: Important: our audit team will need details about change management and how you sign releases.
[03:17] Marco: Our artifacts include signed release manifests and a software bill of materials (SBOM). For air-gap, each patch has a signature and a changelog. You can run the verification locally and we can provide an attest file.
[03:28] Samir: Perf testing — we want to run a benchmark with our workload. Is that possible in your pilot?
[03:32] Marco: Absolutely. Pilot typically includes: a staging cluster on-prem, sample model variant (we can either use an open model you choose or a Redwood-curated model), and a benchmark harness. We'll need sample inputs and expected QPS/latency targets. We can help craft the harness and run tests with your infra.
[03:46] Daniel: Any requirements for the offline benchmark runner? It would need to ingest our private data sets but they can't leave the air-gapped network.
[03:53] Marco: We can deliver the benchmark tool as a signed package for you to run internally. The output logs remain local. We can provide parsing scripts to produce performance reports you can share with internal stakeholders.
[04:05] Priya: What about model licensing? We need clarity if model weights are redistributed or if Redwood hosts them locally.
[04:11] Lina: In Private, model weights are deployed to your infra and are covered under the contract. For certain third-party licensed models, there might be vendor-specific terms; we'll flag those.
[04:20] Karen: Encryption at rest? We need full-disk encryption and also encryption of model weights at rest with keys in our HSM.
[04:25] Marco: We support encrypting model artifacts and storing keys in HSM. The runtime decrypts in-memory on startup and uses a secure memory path. We can provide architecture diagrams for review.
[04:36] Samir: Are there scenarios where Redwood requires connectivity to the cloud for license checks or telemetry?
[04:41] Marco: No license check is required at runtime. All licensing or metering is handled offline for air-gapped deployments. If you choose, metering can be stored locally and an offline invoice package generated for billing reconciliation.
[04:52] Priya: What's the typical timeline from signed contract to pilot?
[04:55] Lina: For air-gapped Private, typical is 6 to 10 weeks: procurement and procurement approvals, hardware provisioning, deployment window, and pilot testing. Faster if you already have hardware and security approvals in place.
[05:06] Daniel: One more — what about Kubernetes? We run OpenShift in production. Does Redwood support OpenShift or do we need a dedicated cluster?
[05:12] Marco: We support both Kubernetes and OpenShift. For air-gapped installs we provide container images and instructions to load them into your private registry. There are tolerance notes for CRI differences; our SEs will validate during the workshop.
[05:24] Karen: On identity, we use SAML 2.0 and corporate SSO. Can we map RBAC roles to AD groups?
[05:29] Marco: Yes, RBAC can integrate with SAML/AD groups. We'll provide a mapping template.
[05:33] Samir: Cost question — is there a difference in pricing between on-prem private and dedicated?
[05:37] Lina: Private typically has a platform license and deployment fee plus optional support tiers. Dedicated is usage/reserved capacity in our cloud and has different unit economics. We'll share pricing bands.
[05:45] Priya: Any blockers you see from your side for an air-gapped pilot?
[05:49] Marco: Practically, the biggest blockers are hardware availability, procurement lead time for approved vendor GPUs, and having a security point-of-contact for HSM integration. If you can share the list of approved vendors and an initial BOM, we can validate fits.
[05:59] Daniel: We'll share vendor list; procurement is already vetting A100 40GB vs 80GB.
[06:03] Lina: Great. Quick recap of next steps: Redwood sends air-gap checklist, sample SBOM + signed update process, pricing bands, and schedules a sizing workshop. Summit will send compliance matrix, vendor list, and perf targets.
[06:15] Karen: We'll also want a deeper security review — can we schedule a SOC2 deep-dive with your security team?
[06:20] Lina: Yes, we can schedule that. I will coordinate with Tara.
[06:24] Samir: That sounds good. Anything else?
[06:26] Marco: One small note — for very constrained racks we have a compact deployment profile that uses model sharding and more aggressive quantization. Perf trade-offs are documented in the sizing guide; we'll include that in the BOM packet.
[06:37] Priya: Perfect. We'll review and come back with dates for the workshop.
[06:40] Lina: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials by Thursday (2025-07-24).
[06:44] Karen: Thanks, bye.
[06:45] Meeting ends

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors (proper nouns sometimes misrecognized). References shared: air-gap checklist (link sent in follow-up), sample SBOM and signed bundle verification tool (will be attached).
